overview: A run of systems moves through the Pacific Northwest this week, with rain and wind early and snow mainly at higher elevations. A building ridge may bring a brief drier spell by the weekend, though its placement is uncertain.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A low pressure system with a cold front brings widespread rain and gusty southeast winds through Tuesday, then another disturbance arrives Wednesday night into Thursday. Snow levels rise above most pass levels by Wednesday evening, so the upper slopes get the snow. Stevens Pass leads at 22", with its biggest day Wednesday. The forecasters say a ridge may bring drier weather for the weekend, but its placement is uncertain.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Periods of rain and mild temperatures dominate through Thursday, with snow mostly confined to the highest terrain early in the week. Whistler has the most snow at 24" and its peak day is Wednesday. The forecast turns to showers Thursday night through Friday. Cypress Mountain sees rain and strong easterly wind on Tuesday.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: A powerful coastal storm brings heavy rain, high winds and some wintry mix to the region around Thanksgiving. Le Massif and Mont-Sainte-Anne each get several inches Thursday and Friday, with Friday as the peak day. Freezing rain or rain is the main precipitation, so snow totals depend on elevation. Blue Mountain in Ontario sees a moderate amount, with its peak on Thursday.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
